candidates.name: Discoid lupus erythematosus
support_spans: The patient denied any trauma history and had no history of connective tissue disease nor any evidence of systemic involvement, such as arthralgia, photosensitivity, or skin rashes.
contradict_spans: The result of a hair pull test was negative.
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin grooves and localized linear hair loss is consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus.

candidates.name: Lichen planopilaris
support_spans: Dermoscopic examination of the alopecic area revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation; however, broken hairs were not seen.
candidates.why: The dermoscopic findings and the presence of lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions are consistent with lichen planopilaris.

candidates.name: Frontal fibrosing alopecia
support_spans: The patient reported that when the lesion had begun approximately 10 years earlier, he had received 2 doses of intralesional steroid via injection on a small bald patch on the vertex.
candidates.why: The patient's history of gradual progression of the lesion and the presence of linear hair loss are consistent with frontal fibrosing alopecia.

key_evidence_spans: The patient denied any trauma history and had no history of connective tissue disease nor any evidence of systemic involvement, such as arthralgia, photosensitivity, or skin rashes.
Dermoscopic examination of the alopecic area revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation; however, broken hairs were not seen.
The patient reported that when the lesion had begun approximately 10 years earlier, he had received 2 doses of intralesional steroid via injection on a small bald patch on the vertex.
Examination revealed 2 long, curved-line, depressed, alopecic patches on the left side of the vertex and frontal scalp area extending to the left eyebrow.
Direct immunofluorescence: Positive with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels
The result of a hair pull test was negative.
Histopathologic examination: Scanning view shows predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis (hematoxylin-eosin staining)
High-power view shows inflammatory infiltrates between adipocytes with hyaline fat necrosis in the subcutis (hematoxylin-eosin staining)
